I then proceeded to the sales floor and located the multi-deck refrigeration system. The case temperature was elevated, with the case temperature at 42°F. I began troubleshooting System #7 and found that the unit was locked out on a high-discharge-pressure safety trip. I checked the discharge pressure and found it operating at approximately 330 PSI. I then verified the discharge pressure safety control and found it set to cut out at 400 PSI. Next, I inspected the condenser coil and found no visible obstructions; however, the condenser fins were damaged in several areas. I also checked the liquid line filter drier for any signs of restriction and found none. After power-cycling the controller to restart the system, the unit tripped again on high discharge pressure. I then performed a thorough cleaning of the condenser coil until the rinse water ran clear. Once cleaning was completed, I restarted the system and monitored operation. After cleaning, the system operated normally and did not trip on high discharge pressure.
